extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: The Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) benchmark is a multimodal dataset designed to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) to recognize and handle conflicting instructions. It comprises 20,000 conflicts evenly distributed across language-language (L-L) and vision-language (V-L) paradigms, spanning eight distinct conflict tasks constructed via an automatic cyclic framework named AutoCreate.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was generated using the AutoCreate framework, an automatic dataset creation framework leveraging programs and large language models (LLMs). Starting from task-relevant input seeds in a seed pool, the framework executes a language loop and a visual loop consisting of an automated Generator, Decorator (introducing contradictions), and Cleaner (excluding data not meeting standards). The dataset underwent quality checks by human experts and LLMs, and refined samples were recycled back into the seed pool across multiple iterations. ImageNet validation set images were retrieved for the SemanticConflict task.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Seed pools generated and expanded via LLMs, programmatically synthesized charts and geometric images, and images sampled from the ImageNet-1k validation set.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For FigureConflict, numerical data was manipulated by changing the maximum value to the minimum value before plotting charts. For GeometricConflict, attribute descriptions (e.g., color and size) were exchanged to refer to non-existent objects. For SemanticConflict, correct class labels in questions were replaced with similar but different objects (e.g., replacing ostrich with kiwi).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The Cleaner module in AutoCreate removes generated data that does not meet established quality standards. Subsets were manually selected and partitioned into SCI-Core (1%), SCI-Base (10%), and SCI-All (100%), with extra effort to ensure diversity in ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, and OCRConflict.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations and evaluations measure whether model responses are conflict-aware (hit ratio). For validation, human experts evaluated model replies to establish a ground truth standard, which was also automated via LLM evaluation agents (e.g., GPT-4, ChatGPT, ChatGLM) using a uniform evaluation prompt.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate were calculated between LLM evaluation agents (GPT-4) and human experts on vision-language conflicts (e.g., GPT-4V showed Spearman's rho of 0.881 and 94% concordance; LLaVA-1.5 showed 0.999 and 99%; Gemini showed 0.854 and 97%).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Provides a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies, promoting inclusivity in AI research, and fostering trust and reliability in AI systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms (excluding other modalities). No fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree. Does not provide a detailed study on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflicting instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) regarding their capability to identify and resolve self-contradictory instructions.
